newsitem.title: JAPAN: Canon sees higher '97 interim parent current prft.
newsitem.headline: Canon sees higher '97 interim parent current prft.

text.p: Canon Inc said on Friday that it expected its parent current profit in the six months to June 30, 1997, to rise from previous year levels.
A Canon spokesman, however, declined to give a specific estimate.
Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Friday that Canon's parent current profit for the half year would rise 23 percent from the previous year to a record 78 billion yen.

It added that the company would post a record high parent current profit of about 145 billion yen for the whole of the 1997 business year if the dollar were to stay at around 115 yen in the second half of the business year.
The paper said the expected profit rise was due to robust sales of copiers and cameras.
In February, Canon said its 1997 full-year parent current profit would be 137 billion yen, compared with an actual 1996 parent current profit of 125.23 billion yen.
